answer: Break voting power away from headcount: weight each account by the square root of its stake before aggregating. One honest participant counts in full, while ten thousand keys sharing one grove of wallets weigh as a single square root, so each extra account adds less influence than the last. Every key must clear a fixed minimum stake before its attestation registers, so an attacker dividing a budget across many identities pushes most below that floor, where their signal is dropped. Splitting is self-defeating; the cheaper route is one deep inlet, competed on quality.
